Table. Data table from tm-interaction-completeness

Completeness here means that the seven rows below exhaust the single-crossing interaction catalogue acting on the transfer matrix: every admissible process is either the identity, one of the two \beta decays, a photon append or remove, or a pair creation or annihilation. Each row is a distinct process, and the final column links back to the operator that defines it in tm-interactions.

# Process Operator Catalogue entry
1 Identity (no interaction) \mathbb{I} trivial pair T_{1,0} \cdot T_{1,0}
2 \beta^- decay (\mathfrak{d} \to \mathfrak{u}) \Delta_\beta = \tfrac{1}{2}(q - q^{-1})\mathbb{I} tm-interactions §1
3 \beta^+ decay (\mathfrak{u} \to \mathfrak{d}) -\Delta_\beta tm-interactions §2
4 Photon absorption (Reidemeister I, append) T_{\gamma e}(q) = T_{pp}(q) tm-interactions §3
5 Photon emission (Reidemeister I, remove) T_{pp}(q)^{-1} tm-interactions §3
6 Pair creation (\gamma\gamma \to e^- e^+) -\Delta_\beta on the affected crossing tm-interactions §4
7 Pair annihilation (e^- e^+ \to \gamma\gamma) \Delta_\beta on the affected crossing tm-interactions §4
